name: Schloss Itter
kurzbeschreibung: Schloss Itter perches on a rocky ridge in the Brixental: origins around 1240, dramatic battle of 1945, and widely visible monument.
beschreibung:
Overview

Steeped in history, Schloss Itter rises prominently on a wooded rocky spur at approximately 665 metres above sea level high above the entrance to the Brixental in the municipality of Itter in the Tyrolean Unterland. Strategically positioned above the confluence of the Brixentaler Ache and Sölllandl, the fortified stronghold guarded the vital trade and border route between Tirol and the Prince-Archbishopric of Salzburg for centuries. Surrounded by lush rolling hills against the prominent silhouette of the Hohe Salve, the castle captivates visitors with its Neo-Gothic architecture and a globally unique history.

History & The Battle for Schloss Itter

The construction of the first border fortification dates back to the early 13th century: around 1240, the castle was first documented as a base of the Bishops of Regensburg before being sold to the Erzbistum Salzburg in 1380. In 1504, the property fell to Emperor Maximilian I. and Tirol. In the 19th century, French piano virtuoso Sophie Menter acquired the estate; luminaries such as Franz Liszt and Pjotr Tschaikowski stayed here as guests. Around 1878, the castle was remodeled in the Neo-Gothic and Romantic styles into a palatial residence featuring Tudor arches, battlements, and decorative gables. The building gained world renown on 5 May 1945 during the legendary Schlacht um Schloss Itter: in the final days of World War II, the castle served as an SS special prison for high-profile French captives (including former prime ministers Édouard Daladier and Paul Reynaud, and General Maurice Gamelin). In an unprecedented historical battle, US Army soldiers fought alongside Wehrmacht soldiers of the Austrian resistance under Major Josef Gangl against attacking Waffen-SS units to rescue the prisoners from execution.

Visit & Arrival

Today, Schloss Itter is privately owned and not open to the general public inside (interior visits are not possible). However, the outdoor grounds, the approach avenue, and the surrounding panoramic hiking trails provide fantastic vantage points of the mighty castle facade and remain freely and freely accessible free of charge throughout the year. A historical memorial plaque in the village of Itter commemorates the liberation of May 1945. Arrival by public transport: By train to Bahnhof Hopfgarten im Brixental or Wörgl Hauptbahnhof, then take VVT bus line 4060 up to Itter (stop Itter Dorfplatz). By car: Via the A12 motorway, exit Wörgl Ost, onto the B178 towards Brixental/St. Johann, then turn off to Itter (parking is available in the village centre near the parish church).

Tips

The scenic circular castle trail around the hill is paved or well-gravelled and ideal for family excursions with strollers and dogs. The castle is best viewed from the vantage point on Dorfstraße and from the panorama terrace of the nearby club hotel. Combine your walk with a trip up the Hohe Salve cable car departing from Hopfgarten.
oeffnungszeiten: Außenansicht & Rundweg ganzjährig frei zugänglich (Schloss privat)
